claim: Mont Gerbier-de-Jonc summit hike is a fairly steep 1.2 km path of about 1h30 round trip from the base car park, and the Sentier des Sources de la Loire is a separate easy 3 km circuit.
quote: The main route is approximately 1.2 km long and requires 1 hour 30 minutes round trip on a fairly steep path. ... The Sentier des Sources de la Loire is a pleasant 3 km walk exploring where the Loire River originates.

claim: Mont Gerbier-de-Jonc peaks at 1551 m and is best visited after snowmelt and bloom; the path is impassable in rain/storm because the trachyte stones turn slippery.
quote: Altitude: 1,551 meters (peak elevation) ... The guide recommends visiting after snow melts and when flowers begin to bloom ... impossible during rain or thunderstorms due to slippery stones.

claim: Mont Mézenc loop from Croix de Peccata is 6.4 km with about 260 m elevation gain, around 2h35, moderate difficulty, reaching the 1747 m summit ridge.
quote: Distance & Duration: 3.98 mi taking approximately 2 hours and 35 minutes ... The trail climbs 856 feet ... The highest point reaches 5,732 feet ... Rated as moderate difficulty ... Starting Location: Parking at Croix de Peccata

claim: Mont Mézenc is the highest peak in the Ardèche at 1753 m (south summit) / 1744 m (north), with a 360° panorama from the Alps to the Puy de Dôme; the standard ascent from the Croix des Boutières car park takes about two hours round trip in summer.
quote: Located at the altitude of 1753 m (5751 feet) for the South Summit, and 1744 m (5722 feet) for the North Summit ... The ascent of Mézenc is easily completed in two hours round trip in the summer, from the Croix des Boutières car park.

claim: Lac de Devesset has an easy 3.5 km loop trail around it, suitable for families on foot or by bike, with supervised swimming only in July–August.
quote: A scenic trail encircles the lake at approximately 3.5 km, noted as an easy walk, accessible to all ... supervised swimming and water sports only operate in the summer (July-August).

claim: Lac de Devesset is a 51-hectare reservoir on the Haut-Vivarais plateau at 1074 m altitude, max depth 10.5 m, dam completed in 1974.
quote: The lake is at 1,074 m altitude ... Its surface area is 51 hectares ... Its maximum depth is 10.5 m (measured in 2011) ... located on the Haut-Vivarais plateau ... The dam was completed in 1974

claim: Mont Chiniac at 1116 m is the easy family belvédère above Saint-Agrève, reachable via the 6 km 'Chante-coucou' loop (+123 m) through the Forêt de la Rèche.
quote: Altitude: 1,116 meters ... The 'Chante-coucou' family hike is described as suitable for families ... Accès libre (free access) year-round ... un point de vue circulaire at the summit with orientation tables

claim: The Chante-coucou loop from Saint-Agrève up Mont Chiniac is a 6 km family hike with 123 m of climb that ends on the Velay / Boutières belvédère.
quote: Cette balade de 6 km et 123 m D+ à faire en famille vous conduira sur le belvédère de la chaîne du Velay et des sucs des Boutières.

claim: The Lignon gorges between Tence and Le Chambon-sur-Lignon are dotted with viewpoints (Moulin de Boyer, Sauron, Beaujeu, Pont de Mars, Pont de Salettes) and six marked PR loops; the upper Lignon is at its wildest near Mazet-Saint-Voy.
quote: Six marked trails available: Pèlerins, Plateau, Pont de Mars, Beaujeu, Papeterie, and Joux circuits. ... 1. Moulin de Boyer (Mazet-Saint-Voy) - wild Lignon near its source

claim: The Haut-Lignon network offers 24 PR loops over ~240 km, including easy options (PR034 Beaujeu 7 km, PR038 Pèlerins 4.9 km) and harder routes (PR033 Lizieux 15.5 km, PR040 Roche druidique 12.8 km).
quote: 24 PR (Promenade & Randonnées) trails totaling approximately 240 km ... PR034 Le Mas de Tencou (Le Mas-de-Tence): 1.7 km, 40 minutes ... PR033 Le circuit du Lizieux (Mazet-Saint-Voy): 15.5 km, 4h 15min

claim: Crêt de l'Oeillon (1364 m) is the second highest summit of the Pilat, with a panorama from the Trois Dents over the Rhône valley as far as the Vercors, Écrins and Mont-Blanc on clear days.
quote: Crêt de l'Oeillon is the second most remarkable summit of the Pilat, standing 1,364 meters above sea level ... on a clear day you can see the Vercors mountains, the Ecrins, and the Mont-Blanc range.

claim: Saint-Bonnet-le-Froid to Les Estables (foot of Mont Mézenc) is roughly 53 km by the scenic cycling route via Mars / Saint-Agrève / Col de la Croix de Peccata (1570 m), implying ~50 minutes by direct car.
quote: The route covers 53,47 km with 1046 m of elevation gain ... via Saint Agrève before tackling the significant climb toward Mont Mézenc ... col de la Croix de Peccata at 1,570 meters

claim: Lalouvesc at 1100 m sits on the junction of the GR420 and GR430 and offers 22+ marked walks, including the 6 km / ~2 h Tour du Mont Chaix loop with Alpine views.
quote: Lalouvesc (at an altitude of 1,100 metres) is the meeting point of the GR® 420 and 430 trails ... More than 22 walks, hikes and thematic trails ... Le tour du Mont Chaix is a hiking circuit ... approximately 6 kilometres represents an average of 2 hours of walking

claim: Les Estables (the village at the foot of Mont Mézenc, with the Croix des Boutières / Peccata trailheads) is less than 30 minutes from Le Puy-en-Velay, confirming snow is the limiting factor since it doubles as a small ski station.
quote: Les Estables, the nearby ski resort at the foot of Mont Mézenc, is less than 30 minutes from Le Puy-en-Velay

claim: The 268 m Passerelle Himalayenne over the Lignon (France's longest, opened April 2022) is accessed from Grazac (5.4 km, +176 m) or Saint-Maurice-de-Lignon (7.7 km, +215 m) — sits in the lower Lignon, ~45 km from Saint-Bonnet so just beyond the 30 km radius.
quote: The Himalayan footbridge is 268.5 m long and 78 m high above the Lignon ... from Grazac (5.4 kilometers round trip with an elevation gain of +176 meters, very easy access) or from Saint-Maurice-de-Lignon (7.7 kilometers, 215 meters of elevation gain)
